     Do not edit — including in Studio; the next build replaces this file. -->

164 event types across 40 resource families. Subscribe an
endpoint to any subset; an endpoint with no list receives all of them.

::note
Delivery succeeds on any 2xx response. A failure is retried up to
6 times, backing off 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h.
::

## `payment_source`

A stored instrument belonging to a customer. These are the events that warn you an instrument will stop working before it does — expiry, an insufficient mandate, an outright refusal.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `payment_source_added` |  |
| `payment_source_updated` |  |
| `payment_source_deleted` |  |
| `payment_source_expiring` | Sent ahead of the expiry date, while the instrument still works, so you can ask the customer to replace it before a renewal fails. |
| `payment_source_expiry_reminder` | Sent on each lead day before a card expires, when the business sets lead days for card expiry (`reminder_config.card_expiring`). Carries `expires_at` and `lead_days`. Emitted once per card, expiry date and lead day. `payment_source_expiring` still fires once, when the card enters its expiry month. |
| `payment_source_mandate_insufficient` | The instrument's authorised per-debit ceiling is below the next amount due on a subscription it is attached to. The ceiling is fixed when the instrument is authorised and cannot be raised in place — only a fresh authorisation from the customer replaces it, so this is a prompt to ask for one. |
| `payment_source_expired` |  |
| `payment_source_role_changed` |  |
| `payment_source_invalidated` | The instrument was refused in a way that will not resolve on its own and has been marked unusable. Distinct from expiry: nothing ran out, it was declined. |

## `subscription`

The life of one subscription, from creation through each renewal to cancellation, including changes scheduled ahead of time and the reminders sent before they take effect.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `subscription_created` |  |
| `subscription_started` |  |
| `subscription_activated` |  |
| `subscription_changed` |  |
| `subscription_change_scheduled` |  |
| `subscription_scheduled_change_removed` |  |
| `subscription_renewed` |  |
| `subscription_renewal_skipped` |  |
| `subscription_skip_scheduled` |  |
| `subscription_scheduled_skip_removed` |  |
| `subscription_trial_ending` | Sent on each of the business's lead days before a trial ends, with `lead_days` on the event. |
| `subscription_cancel_scheduled` |  |
| `subscription_scheduled_cancellation_removed` |  |
| `subscription_canceled` |  |
| `subscription_paused` |  |
| `subscription_pause_scheduled` |  |
| `subscription_resumed` |  |
| `subscription_resumption_scheduled` |  |
| `subscription_reactivated` |  |
| `subscription_deleted` |  |
| `subscription_renewal_reminder` | Sent on each of the business's lead days before a renewal (`reminder_config`), with `lead_days` on the event. Emitted once per subscription, renewal date and lead day, so it is safe to act on directly. |
| `subscription_cancellation_reminder` | Sent on each of the business's lead days before a scheduled cancellation takes effect, with `lead_days` on the event. |
| `subscription_pause_reminder` | Sent on each of the business's lead days before a scheduled pause (`reminder_config.pause`), with `pause_at`, `lead_days` and `scheduled_change` on the event. Off by default. |
| `subscription_resume_reminder` | Sent on each of the business's lead days before a scheduled resume (`reminder_config.resume`), with `resume_at`, `lead_days` and `scheduled_change` on the event. Off by default. |
| `subscription_pre_debit_notification` | Advance notice of a mandate debit, carrying the amount, the date and the mandate reference. Required before every debit on some rails, and sent by the platform because the gateway does not send it. |

## `invoice`

|---|---|
| `invoice_generated` |  |
| `invoice_pending_created` |  |
| `invoice_closed` |  |
| `invoice_updated` |  |

| `invoice_payment_due` |  |
| `invoice_payment_due_reminder` | Sent on each of the business's lead days before the due date of an open invoice that is not collected automatically (`reminder_config.payment_due`), with `due_at` and `lead_days` on the event. Off by default. |
| `invoice_not_paid` |  |
| `invoice_voided` |  |
| `invoice_written_off` |  |
| `invoice_deleted` |  |
| `invoice_dunning_started` |  |
| `invoice_dunning_exhausted` | The retry sequence for an unpaid invoice has run out of attempts. No further collection will be tried automatically. |
| `invoice_dunning_stopped` |  |
| `invoice_dunning_reminder` |  |

## `credit_note`

| `credit_note_created` |  |

## `payment`

An attempt to collect money and how it ended. `payment_authentication_required` is the one outcome that is neither success nor failure.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `payment_initiated` |  |
| `payment_succeeded` |  |
| `payment_failed` |  |
| `payment_authentication_required` | The debit was accepted but the rail has paused it pending the buyer's additional authentication. Neither a success nor a failure: the money moves only if the buyer authenticates, and nothing else will prompt them. |

## `refund`

Money on its way back to the payer, reported twice: once when accepted, once when settled.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `refund_created` | The provider has ACCEPTED the refund. On cards and bank rails the money lands days later, so treat this as an instruction in flight rather than an outcome. |
| `refund_settled` | The refund actually went through, confirmed by the provider. This is the one to pay out or notify on. |
| `refund_failed` |  |

## `transaction`

|---|---|

| `transaction_reconciled` |  |
| `transaction_late_failure` | A transaction that had been reported as successful was later reversed by the provider. |

## `payment_attempt`

## `receipt`

A numbered record of money received: one per payment, or one per payment on a payment request. Sent when the receipt gets its number, which is within seconds of the payment.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `receipt_created` | Carries the receipt number, the amount received and what it was applied to. A receipt never changes after this event. |

## `payment_request`

A request for several open invoices of one customer, paid by one charge or one link. Each invoice still gets its own payment and its own `payment_succeeded`, which names the request.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `payment_request_created` |  |
| `payment_request_paid` | Every invoice in the request is settled. Sent once, after the child `payment_succeeded` events. |
| `payment_request_payment_failed` | The charge for the request failed or was reversed. The request is open again and the customer was sent the link. |
| `payment_request_canceled` |  |
| `payment_request_expired` |  |

## `feature`

A capability in your catalogue that a plan can grant, such as single sign-on or a project limit. Use these events to refresh any entitlements your app caches.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `feature_created` |  |
| `feature_updated` |  |
| `feature_archived` | The feature no longer grants anything: it leaves every subscription's entitlements and its checks answer `feature_archived`. Grants are kept, and reactivating the feature sends `feature_updated` with `active: true`. |

## `plan_entitlement`

What a product grants for one feature. A change here alters the entitlements of every subscription on that product.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `plan_entitlement_set` | Sent when a grant is created or its value changes. The payload carries `value` and `previous_value`, which is null for a new grant. |

## `subscription_entitlement`

A per-subscription override of what its plan grants for one feature.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `subscription_entitlement_set` | Sent when an override is created or its value changes. The payload carries `value` and `previous_value`, which is null for a new override. |

## `usage_event`

Usage events you sent. We do not send one webhook for each event; this family reports on them in summary.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `usage_event_unmatched` | Sent at most once an hour when events arrived with a customer key that no customer has. Add the key to a customer and the events bill. |

## `model_prices`

The AI model price list. Sent when a list price that your meters use changes.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `model_prices_changed` | Sent once per price sync to each business whose meters used a changed model in the last 35 days. Each change gives the old and new price, the time the new price starts, and two flags: `bill_moves` (a live subscription bills that model from the list) and `cost_moves` (you have no cost of your own for it). Usage before the start time keeps the old price. |

## `credit_grant`

Credit that a customer holds, in money or in your credit unit. Invoices use it in a fixed order, and it can expire.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `credit_grant_created` |  |
| `credit_grant_applied` | Sent once for each invoice that used credit grants. It lists each grant and the amount that the invoice used. |
| `credit_grant_expired` |  |
| `credit_grant_voided` |  |
| `credit_grant_restored` | A voided invoice gave its credit back. When the grant had expired, the credit comes back as a new grant that expires in 12 months. |
| `credit_grant_activated` |  |

An amount of credit that your app reserved before a call. We send these events only to an endpoint that lists them by name.

## `spend_limit`

A spend limit on a customer, a subscription or a usage property. Sent once per limit, subject and interval when spend reaches the limit.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `spend_limit_reached` | Carries the limit, the subject, the interval, the amount spent and when the interval resets. `mode` is `hard` (new requests are refused) or `soft` (notice only). |

## `customer_limit_tier`

A limit tier that a customer reached when its total paid amount grew. A tier never goes down after a refund.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `customer_limit_tier_reached` |  |

## `usage_alert`

An alert on usage, spend, credit balance or credit runway. Each threshold triggers at most once per period and resolves once.

| Event type | |
|---|---|
| `usage_alert_triggered` |  |
| `usage_alert_resolved` | The value moved back across a threshold, or the period ended (`reason: period_ended`). Each trigger has exactly one resolve. |
